paragraphs: LAB 2 • PREPARATION • 4 MINUTES • ONE PER AUTHOR
Give each reviewer the same task and starting state. Ask for a result; let them choose the steps.
Author ____________________   Tool / version ____________________   Group ____   Letter A / B / C / D
1  User and goal  Who is this for? What do they need to do, and why?
2  Task to read aloud  Write one short task. Include the starting input and what must stay unchanged.
3  Success  What visible result will you check?
4  Ready to repeat  How will you reset? What will you show if the tool cannot run?
Example task: “Try this texture set on the target crate. Leave the protected crate unchanged.”
Ready check: prepared copies • same version • start state ready • reset ready
Choose a mode: hands-on / recording / paper or Figma. A prototype can test understanding; it cannot verify engine behavior.
LAB 2 • PEER REVIEW • ONE SHEET PER REVIEWER
Reviewer: try the task and say what you expect. Author: watch first. Record any help you give.
Mode: hands-on / recording / paper or Figma     Result: independent / helped / blocked / execution untested
1  Task  What result are you trying to reach?
2  Evidence  What did you do, expect and observe? Where did you need help?
Use a lens that fits your observation. You do not need to answer every question.

Know the task — Is the goal and scope clear?
Guide the eye — Do grouping, spacing and contrast show what matters?
Make actions clear — Can you tell what to click and what state it is in?
Keep a shared visual language — Do labels, colors and controls mean the same thing?
Test the whole workflow — Can you check the result and recover?
3  Keep and improve  One observed strength. One issue or question that matters, and why.
If no issue appeared, say so. Mark anything you could not test. Give this sheet to the author.
10-minute round: task 0:00 • try 0:30 • record and share 2:30 • swap 4:00 • finish and reset 8:00
LAB 2 • REFLECTION • FINAL 5 MINUTES • ONE PER AUTHOR
Compare your reviews. Preserve a strength, choose one change, and plan a test.
Author ____________________   Distinct reviewers ____   Modes used ____________________
1  Keep  Which strength did a reviewer observe?
2  Prioritize  Which issue or uncertainty matters most? Cite a peer’s observation and its consequence.
3  Revise  What specific change will you make or investigate?
4  Retest  State the input, action and expected result. Include what must stay unchanged.
5  Reflect  What changed or strengthened your judgment? What is still untested?
A serious failure can matter even if only one reviewer sees it. Record the reviews you actually received.
LAB 1 STUDENT HANDOUT   8 MINUTES   FICTIONAL CASE
Decide what the tool should do before seeing its output. Then use evidence to identify one issue and design a retest. No coding or installation is needed.
Group ______   Reader ______   Recorder ______   Evidence checker ______   Reporter ______

paragraphs: INSTRUCTOR GUIDE   1 OF 2

Use the fictional renamer to establish evidence-based review before teaching UX vocabulary. Students compare a stated contract with visible behavior, then propose a test. Accept different priorities when the reasoning is supported.
INSTRUCTOR GUIDE   2 OF 2

Protect task preparation and complete attempts. Form groups of four, assign A–D, and keep tools on their prepared machines. Each pair tests in both directions. The later letter tests the earlier letter’s tool first.
Call every round: 0:00 state task; 0:30 attempt; 2:30 record; 3:30 explain; 4:00 swap; 4:30 attempt; 6:30 record; 7:30 explain; 8:00 finish and reset; 10:00 switch.
tables: Distribute one group sheet. Assign reader, recorder, evidence checker and reporter. Read the rule.
Individual prediction. Do not reveal results.
Compare expected names as a group. Check that protected scope is explicit.
Record what evidence would establish success.
Open reveal.html. Display the fictional “Success: 4 assets updated” message and results.
Write one supported finding and a retest.
Two 20-second reports, then 20 seconds for questions.
The output violates both protected scope and the exactly-one-prefix rule. The success count alone proves neither. Internal cause, Undo, a second run and performance remain unknown.
With only the three crates selected, I expected barrel_D to stay unchanged, but it became SM_barrel_D. This changes unrelated work.
Restore all four starting names; select only the crates; run once; inspect all four expected names above. Then propose a separate second-run test. Do not claim that test has occurred.
Prioritize scope because unrelated work changes, or the duplicate prefix because it violates the naming contract. Ask for the consequence and supporting observation, not a preferred phrase.
Which preview evidence could expose the mistake before Apply? What does a success message omit? Revisit first judgments during UX, then carry input/action/evidence/protected scope into peer review.
Prepare one bounded task and a fallback.
Brief roles and modes, confirm letters and answer questions.
Read reviews; choose priority, revision and retest; record changed judgment.
Per student: preparation page, three copies of review page, synthesis page. One Lab 1 sheet per group. Display dashboard.html. Example for 24: six groups, 72 review sheets; roster is not assumed.
“What did you expect, what happened, and why does it matter?” Record author help. A strength needs evidence too. If no fault is observed, propose a test rather than invent a defect.
Allow at most one minute of troubleshooting within the attempt, then declare blocked and switch to recording or concept. Stop risks to real work. No software installation during rounds.
Trio: A–B, A–C, B–C; third observes, each gets two distinct reviews. Five: A–B/C–D; A–C/B–E; A–D/C–E. A/C get three; B/D/E get two. Do not count observers or repeated partners as new reviewers.
End UX at 5:16. If late, state the reduced number of complete rounds honestly; retain five minutes of synthesis. Full staff scripts and additional attendance cases are in facilitator.html.

paragraphs: LIVE UNREAL RUN SHEET   1 OF 4   SETUP

Place the prepared classroom fountain at three tagged anchors. Separate predictable placement from runtime performance: a bounded batch does not establish a frame-time budget.

Preset review: one lightweight GPU sprite emitter, 90 particles/second, lifetime 1.4–1.75 seconds, sprite size 6–12 cm, default Niagara sprite material. Three new effects maximum; scale 0.25–1; anchors at least 100 cm apart. Effect Type: 5000 cm distance, maximum 4 instances per system and 8 overall. This classroom review does not certify packaged-game performance.
LIVE UNREAL RUN SHEET   4 OF 4   RECOVERY
Use one short recovery attempt, then switch to the prepared browser walkthrough. State what is observed and what is still unverified. Do not spend the peer-review time debugging the editor.
tables: Prepare the live Material and VFX demo

Launch Scripts/launch_live_demo.ps1 from Week07UnrealPython. It opens W07_MaterialVFXLab and runs the non-destructive preflight. If this project is already open, use its existing editor and Tools > Material & VFX Tools.

Two plain cubes, three empty pedestals, no placed effects. The near cube is W07_Crate_Target; the far cube is W07_Crate_Protected. Both use the same shared mesh. Open the map from Content/Week07/Maps if needed.

Select W07_Crate_Target in the Outliner. In Content/Week07/LiveDemo/Textures select all three T_Crate textures: BaseColor, Normal and ORM. Content Browser selection and level selection are separate. Wait for browser selection to update before Preview.

Tools > Material & VFX Tools. Material Setup, slot 0, fresh MI_ name such as MI_Crate_Live_01. Do not overwrite an existing instance. For PySide: Python console: import week07_tools as w7; w7.show_assistants().

Open live-demo.html in a browser before teaching. It contains actual baseline, material, VFX and native-panel captures, plus read-aloud prompts. It works offline without Unreal or Qt. If a failure persists beyond 30 seconds, use it within the same demo slot.
Show both cubes. “They share a mesh. Which one should change, and what must remain untouched?” Point to the selected target and three textures.
Choose Material Setup, slot 0 and a fresh MI_ name. Preview. Read the destination, parent, three texture mappings and one target. “Preview has not changed the scene.”
Apply once. Show the near blue cube and far plain cube. Check the instance parent and texture parameters if time permits. “A success message needs a visible scope check.”
Try Preview again with the same output name. It must block overwrite. “What should happen on a repeat?”
Use Edit > Undo only when its label identifies the material assignment. Target returns to plain. The new instance remains. Explain that assignment Undo and asset cleanup are separate.
Leave the unsaved draft for later inspection; use a fresh name next time. Ask one student to state input, action, expected result and protected scope.
Select W07_VFXAnchor_1, _2 and _3. Choose VFX Placement, classroom fountain, scale 1.0. “How many effects should this create, and where?”
Preview: three anchors, three effects, their positions and rotations. Apply once. Show three visible fountains.
Reselect the same anchors if necessary. Preview again: occupied anchors must block repeated placement. “The tool checks duplication before mutation.”
Edit > Undo the known VFX placement. Verify all three effects disappear; pedestals remain. If Undo label is unfamiliar, stop and use recovery instructions.
Ask: “What have we verified? What remains unmeasured?” Answer: placement and recovery checked; runtime performance on target hardware remains unmeasured. Hand off at 4:02.
Read the message. Check target + textures separately, slot 0, valid fresh MI_ name, or three tagged anchors. Preview again.
Show the captured preview and ask students to identify scope.
Restore intended selection and Preview again. Apply consumes the old plan even when blocked.
Discuss why the old plan should expire.
Use a new MI_ name; for effects, Undo the known previous batch. Do not overwrite assets or pile on effects.
Native: Reconnect, then Preview. PySide: close and reopen using w7.show_assistants().
Use the other UI only if already prepared; otherwise browser.
Stop. Inspect target and protected cube, output asset and placed Actors. Failed material setup restores assignments but may retain a draft. Do not Save All.
Describe the uncertainty; use verified captured states.
Do not issue repeated Undo blindly. Reopen the saved W07_MaterialVFXLab and decline saving only the rehearsal map edits. Inspect any new instance separately.
Switch to live-demo.html. No engine, Qt, network or installation is needed.
Use prediction, observed result, repeat block and recovery prompts.

Do not save the changed demo map. Reopen its saved baseline and verify two plain cubes and zero effects. New instance cleanup is separate: inspect references before deleting only your rehearsal asset. Never delete the Generated folder as a reset.

UE 5.7.4 material creation/readback, protected cube/shared mesh unchanged, material Undo with asset retained, three exact VFX placements, duplicate block, VFX Undo, invalid/missing/stale selections, live PySide workflows and reopening. Native UI Preview/Apply is checked separately in the evidence report.

Actual editor results and discrete screenshots establish this fixture workflow. They do not establish every possible asset, target-machine performance, or a packaged-game result. See the rehearsal report beside the fallback captures for the recorded checks.
